security_audit.summary: The skill is a RunComfy CLI guide for Nano Banana 2 image editing. Confirmed risks are limited to expected external CLI execution, remote API submission, and credential handling. Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, and token-path documentation caused several false positives; no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution and package installation
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running npx, npm, or runcomfy commands. Pin trusted CLI versions where possible.
Tell users that prompts and image URLs are sent to RunComfy. Avoid private images unless the user accepts that transfer.
Do not read or print the token file. Prefer secret managers or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in CI environments.

content.user_title: Edit Images with Nano Banana on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image editors need reliable subject preservation and batch edits without building API calls by hand. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through RunComfy Nano Banana Edit.
actual_capabilities: Invokes the RunComfy Nano Banana 2 edit endpoint through the local CLI.
Accepts 1-20 public HTTPS image URLs for image-to-image edits.
Documents prompt, aspect ratio, resolution, seed, safety, and output format options.
Provides examples for background swaps, batch edits, and spatial object edits.
Explains when to choose GPT Image 2 edit, Flux Kontext, or Nano Banana text-to-image.
Documents authentication, exit codes, output downloads, and expected network endpoints.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account, local CLI installation, and a valid token.
Prompts and image URLs are submitted to a remote RunComfy service.
Public HTTPS image URLs are required for model input.
Long compound edit prompts can cause visual drift.

use_cases.title: Create consistent product galleries
use_cases.description: Batch edit product images with locked framing, resolution, and background style.

use_cases.title: Swap portrait backgrounds
use_cases.description: Preserve face, pose, and clothing while changing the scene behind the subject.

use_cases.title: Localize visual edits
use_cases.description: Remove or change one object with spatial instructions while preserving the rest of the image.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit on this image URL: [image URL]. Keep the subject identity, pose, and clothing unchanged. Change only the background to [new background].

prompt_templates.title: Product Batch Refresh
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit for these product image URLs: [image URLs]. Keep each product shape, label, and crop unchanged. Replace the background with [studio style]. Use the same aspect ratio and resolution for all outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Spatial Object Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit on this image URL: [image URL]. Keep everything unchanged except [specific object and location]. Change that object to [desired result].

prompt_templates.title: Seeded Creative Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit on these campaign image URLs: [image URLs]. Keep brand elements and composition unchanged. Generate [number] variants with seed [seed] and output format [format]. Change only [controlled creative variable].

output_examples.input: A portrait image URL with a request to keep the person unchanged and replace the background.
output_examples.output: An edited portrait where the face, pose, and clothing remain stable while the background changes to the requested scene.

output_examples.input: Three product image URLs with a request for one shared studio background and square framing.
output_examples.output: A consistent product set with matching background style, crop, resolution, and preserved labels.

output_examples.input: A still-life image URL with a request to remove only the leftmost object.
output_examples.output: An edited image where the target object is removed and the remaining objects, table, and lighting stay intact.

best_practices: State what must stay unchanged before describing the edit.
Use spatial language for local changes, such as left object or upper-right corner.
Lock aspect ratio and resolution when editing a batch.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated edits in one prompt.
Do not use private images unless the user accepts remote processing.
Do not change aspect ratio unless cropping or stretching is acceptable.

faq.question: Does this skill edit images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to submit edits to the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: You need one to twenty public HTTPS image URLs and a clear edit prompt.

faq.question: Can it process batches?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented endpoint accepts up to twenty input images per call.

faq.question: Does it preserve identity?
faq.answer: The skill focuses on prompts that preserve identity, pose, clothing, brand details, and framing.

faq.question: When should I choose another model?
faq.answer: Use GPT Image 2 for multilingual in-image text, Flux Kontext for precise single-reference edits, and Nano Banana text-to-image for new images.

faq.question: How are credentials handled?
faq.answer: RunComfy login stores a local token, or CI can use RUNCOMFY_TOKEN instead.
